t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section drawn as one engineering drawing sheet on warm limestone paper, framed by a fine navy border, with a gridded title block at the bottom-right corner. Top-left: a small mono eyebrow and a very large light-weight navy sans headline. Left: a wide orthographic front elevation of white polypropylene process equipment in uniform navy hairlines, no shading, with dimension chains above and below. Right: a narrow column of numbered mono drawing notes for <CONTENT>, beside a hairline rule. Flat, square corners, lots of empty paper.
signature_idea: The section is the drawing sheet: deliverables are written as numbered drawing notes beside a dimensioned elevation, signed off in a title block.
strengths: directly expresses 'engineering documents' as the deliverable
very calm: one ink, lots of paper, light headline
numbered notes are a clean, buildable list pattern
title block is a distinctive, brand-specific closing device
weaknesses: elevation is generic process equipment that reads as stainless vessels on legs, not PP
no steel-blue accent, so nothing leads the eye
dimension chains carry blank or meaningless labels
drawing and notes are not linked, notes do not reference parts of it
brand_fit_why: Limestone paper, navy hairlines, light headline, mono notes and square framing are on-brand and calm; only the missing accent and generic vessels hold it back slightly.
